text:
**Short answer: yes at about $450 or less if you want an AC-heavy, outage-and-camping unit. At $499, newer models are worth a look first.**

**What's good**
- **Real capacity:** Independent tests measured about 950-1,030 Wh out of the rated 1,152 Wh (82-90%) ([Watt Power Station](https://wattpowerstation.com/power-stations/bluetti-ac180/), [PCWorld](https://www.pcworld.com/article/1966571/bluetti-ac180-power-station-review.html)).
- **Output:** 1,800W continuous, with a 2,700W "Power Lifting" mode. That mode is only for resistive loads like heaters and kettles ([Best Batteries](https://us.best-batteries.com/reviews/bluetti-ac180/)).
- **Battery and warranty:** LiFePO4 rated for 3,500+ cycles, plus a 5-year warranty ([BLUETTI](https://www.bluettipower.com/products/ac180?variant=44099774480603)).
- **Charging:** About 1.3-1.8 hours from the wall in Turbo mode ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/reviews/camping-and-hiking/power-station/bluetti-ac180)).
- **Extras:** A 15W wireless charging pad and app control.

**What's not**
- **Weight:** It's heavy for its capacity, at about 36 lb.
- **Small loads:** Efficiency drops a lot on them. Outdoor Life measured only 54% of rated capacity at a ~34W load, so it's a poor fit for a CPAP or fridge overnight ([Watt Power Station](https://wattpowerstation.com/power-stations/bluetti-ac180/)).
- **DC efficiency:** PCWorld measured only 71% on a USB-PD load ([iTechGuides](https://www.itechguides.com/bluetti-ac180-power-station-review-excellent-ac-efficiency-but-heavy-and-less-impressive-over-dc/)).
- **Fan noise:** The fan is audible while charging and under load.
- **Heat:** Output can drop to 1,500W in hot weather (95-104°F) ([Best Batteries](https://us.best-batteries.com/reviews/bluetti-ac180/)).
- **UPS use:** It's only 20ms, so OutdoorGearLab wouldn't trust it for sensitive electronics.
- **Expansion:** Sources conflict. Bluetti's page touts the B80/B230/B300 batteries, but they only top it up in Power Bank Mode, and one tester says it takes no extra batteries. Don't buy it counting on expansion.

**Price and alternatives**
- It's listed at $499 on [BLUETTI's US store](https://www.bluettipower.com/products/ac180?variant=44099774480603) and $449 on Amazon as of Oct 24 ([iTechGuides](https://www.itechguides.com/bluetti-ac180-power-station-review-excellent-ac-efficiency-but-heavy-and-less-impressive-over-dc/)). Some pages showed it limited or discontinued, so check stock.
- Dealectric, an affiliate site, reports code AFF5OFF took $24.95 off at BLUETTI's cart on Oct 21 ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180)). Confirm it at checkout.
- OutdoorGearLab calls the successor, the Bluetti Elite 100 V2, a better product: 25 lb, quieter, faster charging, and 1,024Wh. It lists around $489 ([Watt Power Station](https://wattpowerstation.com/power-stations/bluetti-ac180/)). OutdoorGearLab also prefers the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (about $500), and the EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic (about $499) tested at 93% efficiency. I don't have purchase links for those from these results.

**Bottom line:** Buy the AC180 if you find it at $449 or less and mostly run AC appliances, tools, or short outages, and the weight doesn't bother you. If you'll carry it often or run small loads for long stretches, compare the Elite 100 V2 first.
